newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank hikes repo rate by 70 bps to 9.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank hikes repo rate by 70 bps to 9.7 pct.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Wednesday said it had raised its bill repurchase rate by 70 basis points to 9.7 percent, but left the reverse repo rate unchanged at 7.2 percent.
The NBS announced the rise in a statement to markets but officials were not immediately available to comment.

The repo hike followed the Finance Ministry's 273-day treasury bill auction earlier on Wednesday, the average yield for which hit 9.669 percent, up from 9.307 percent in the last auction of similar bills.
Money market dealers said they had expected the repo hike which seemed logical considering a further increase in the T-bill yield.

"The repo hike had been expected, though I personally expected it rather next week, and it has pushed the interbank money market offered rates ceiling up to 16 percent from the previous 15 percent," Jaroslav Hora of VUB Bank told Reuters.
"The market rates will certainly rise now," he added.
The NBS's last-resort lending facility, the Lombard, currently stands at 15 percent.
The market offered rates quotations ranged from 13.0-14.8 percent for all terms.
